# Skill Frontmatter Invariants

SKILL.md frontmatter keys interact across two permission layers: the skill's own `capabilities` / `allowed-tools` declarations, and Claude Code's per-agent-type tool allowlist. When the two disagree, the agent-type allowlist wins — silently. Agents that declare write capability but dispatch through a read-only agent type produce correct output and then refuse to persist it.

## The invariant

When a skill declares write capability — either `capabilities.write_files: true` OR `allowed-tools` listing `Write`/`Edit` — it MUST NOT set `agent:` to a type that excludes those tools.

Allowed: omit the `agent:` key (skill runs in the caller's context), or set `agent:` to a write-capable type (`general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork`).

## Agent type tool allowlists

| Agent type | Write / Edit / NotebookEdit | Use for |
|------------|-----------------------------|---------|
| `general-purpose`, `claude`, `fork` | ✓ all tools | Skills that author files |
| `Plan` | ✗ excluded | Read-only planning / exploration |
| `Explore` | ✗ excluded | Read-only codebase analysis |
| `loa-scout`, `prompt-auditor`, `prompt-auditor-io` | ✗ excluded | Read-only project agents (`.claude/agents/`) |
| (unset) | inherited from caller | Default; safe for write-capable skills |

Source: Claude Code agent-type definitions in the system prompt, and `.claude/agents/*.md`.

## Enforcement

`.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh` checks this invariant on every SKILL.md. A violation exits with code 1 and message:

> agent type '<name>' excludes Write/Edit tools but skill declares write capability …

The allowlist is maintained in `.claude/data/agent-types.yaml` (one `write_capable` flag per agent type); the script loads the `true` entries into `WRITE_CAPABLE_AGENTS` and falls back to `general-purpose` alone when the file is missing, unparsable, or lists no `write_capable: true` entry. Adding a new write-capable agent type is intentionally a one-line edit with reviewer visibility.

## Mechanical C-PROC-001 enforcement via `disallowed-tools` (cycle-114 FR-4)

`disallowed-tools` frontmatter (Claude Code ≥2.1.152) removes tools from the
model while a skill is active — a harness-level barrier that instructions
cannot override. Cycle-114 uses it to make C-PROC-001 ("NEVER write application
code outside `/implement`") mechanical for review skills rather than prose-only.

| Skill class | `disallowed-tools` | Why |
|-------------|--------------------|-----|
| Pure-review (`write_files: false`, no report artifacts) | `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit` | Never writes anything — remove the write tools outright |
| Sprint review/audit (`reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit` | Write STATE-zone feedback/checkmarks/COMPLETED markers, run the allowed verdict check and run `adversarial-review.sh` (forks the provider CLIs, appends the `.run` cost and MODELINV ledgers, moves the previous round's a2a envelope aside as `.prev`, writes the new one; review also runs `qmd-context-query.sh`); System remains `none` and App remains `read` |
| Report-authoring review (`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`; `write_files: true`) | `NotebookEdit`, `Bash(git add/commit/push *)` | Legitimately write STATE-zone reports/vision/lore, so `Write` is retained; app-code prevention is governed by **zones**, and the implementation-only git mutations are removed |

**`REVIEW_WRITE_EXCEPTIONS`** (in `validate-skill-capabilities.sh`):
`red-teaming`, `bridgebuilder-review`, `spiraling`, `autonomous-agent`,
`run-bridge`, `run-mode`, `reviewing-code`, `auditing-security`. These `role: review` skills keep `Write` by design —
the adversarial/report authors write STATE-zone artifacts, and the autonomous
orchestrators dispatch implementation through the harness (which runs inside
`/implement`, where writes are sanctioned). The validator emits a WARN for any *other* `role: review`
skill that declares `write_files: true` without disallowing `Write` — surfacing
a new C-PROC-001 gap at lint time. `disallowed-tools` is tool-granular, not
path-granular; it cannot express "no `src/` writes but yes `grimoires/` writes",
which is why report-authoring skills rely on zones for path-level control.

Applies to every `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`. The lint runs as part of the normal validation suite (`bats tests/unit/skill-capabilities.bats`).

# Git Stash Safety

`git stash push / pop` wraps are risky inside Loa skill execution: pre-commit hooks run their own internal `git stash --keep-index`, an overlapping outer stash shifts the indexes, and `pop` can land on the wrong entry. Combined with output-swallowing (`| tail -N`, `|| true`, `2>/dev/null`) this produces silent data loss that looks like success.

**Mechanically enforced since cycle-122**: `block-destructive-bash.sh` pattern `FR-1.2b` BLOCKS `git stash push/pop/apply` combined with `| tail`/`| head`, `|| true`, or `2>/dev/null` in the same statement — the block message is the repair prompt. This file keeps only the interface and the judgment rules a fence cannot express.

## The safe interface

```bash
source .claude/scripts/stash-safety.sh
stash_with_guard "pre-check" -- run_linter src/   # count-delta enforced, full output surfaced, exit propagated
```

Or sidestep stashing entirely with a worktree (no index-shift window):

```bash
worktree_path="$(mktemp -d)/loa-check"
git worktree add "$worktree_path" HEAD
(cd "$worktree_path" && run_linter src/)
git worktree remove "$worktree_path"
```

## Judgment rules the fence cannot express

- MUST NOT combine `git stash -k` with pre-commit-wrapped operations (the internal `--keep-index` collision is invisible to a command-string fence) — use a worktree.
- SHOULD reach for `git fsck --unreachable | grep commit` BEFORE any `git gc` when recovery is needed — orphaned stashes survive in the object DB only until the next prune.

## Origin

- Defect: [#555](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/555) — 4 Edit-tool NOTES.md updates lost to the hazard pattern; recovered only because `git gc --prune=now` hadn't run. Tracker: [#557](https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa/issues/557).
- The hazard shape recurred live during cycle-122 itself (a `git stash pop >/dev/null 2>&1` during a baseline check — caught, verified lossless, and turned into the FR-1.2b fence the same day).

## Related rules

- [shell-conventions.md](shell-conventions.md) — heredoc safety, strict-mode patterns.
- [zone-system.md](zone-system.md) — `.claude/` framework boundary (Bash writes now fenced by FR-SZ2).

I found 7 defects, ranked by severity below; one more claim is unverified. To run the tests I worked on copies in `~/rv`, because `/tmp` is mounted noexec and the frozen tree has lost the script's 100755 mode. `evals/graders/no-secrets.sh` isn't in the snapshot (base or head), so I stood in a stub that greps for secret patterns. With those changes, SC-1 to SC-6 all pass, but several of them pass for the wrong reason or cannot fail.

**1. `head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:159-161` — SC-6 "a non-record fixture is refused" never reaches the guard it claims to test, and the run wipes the template dir.**
- The guard at `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295` only fires when `fixture.yaml` exists. The test's `pr-01` has only the two instruction files (lines 37-38), so the check is skipped.
- Seeding then continues, `shutil.rmtree(fdir)` (line 730) deletes `pr-01`, and line 745 copies the templates out of that same `pr-01` directory.
- Evidence: on a copy the run exited 1 with `FileNotFoundError: .../corpus/pr-01/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Afterwards `pr-01` held only `PR.md`, `base/`, `head/` and `head.diff`; the instruction templates were gone.
- So the test passes on a traceback, not a refusal. It also shows that any `pr-NN` directory without a `fixture.yaml` (including the template source `pr-01`) is deleted without a check.

**2. `head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69`, `:90`, `:91`, `:143` — these `! cmd` assertions can never fail.**
- Bats runs tests under `set -e`, which ignores a pipeline negated with `!`, and none of these lines is the last command in its test. Bats 1.13.0 here confirms it: `! true` followed by more commands passes.
- Line 69 (previous-round section never read): I changed `SKIP_SECTION` so the "Previous Feedback Status" section is parsed. `pr-90.dropped.txt` then contained "must never be read", and SC-1 still passed.
- Line 90 (no file carries the fake key), line 91 (c.sh is not a label) and line 143 (no stale corpus row) are equally inert. They need `run !` or a `[ ... ]` / `if` form.

**3. `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:261-264` — a failed `--approve` leaves the corpus inconsistent.**
- The labels file is rewritten with the new `# approved-by:` header before `build_manifest` validates it.
- If validation fails (e.g. a hand-curated `must_match` is not unique), the TSV says approved, the manifest still says `approved: false`, and SHA256SUMS is stale.
- Reproduced: approve exited 1, the header read `lead 2026-10-14`, the manifest still had `approved=false`, and `--check` then failed with `SHA256SUMS mismatch: labels/pr-90.tsv`.

**4. `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312` — binary files renamed inside a directory slip past the binary filter.**
- `git diff --numstat -M` prints `d/{a.bin => b.bin}`. `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")` turns that into `b.bin`, but name-status gives `d/b.bin`, so the check at line 321 misses.
- Verified with a throwaway repo. The file is then copied through `redact()` (line 125), whose `decode('utf-8','replace')` corrupts the binary bytes in `base/` and `head/`.

**5. `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:45-46` vs `:710-728` — the header promises a no-secrets scan of every written file; the no-label path skips it.**
- The header says "every written file passes evals/graders/no-secrets.sh or the seed fails".
- The no-label branch writes `labels/<fx>.dropped.txt` and `corpus.tsv` and freezes without calling `scan()`. In the normal path, the task YAMLs and `corpus.tsv` (lines 784, 796) are also written outside the scan.

**6. `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:37-39` vs `:418-459` — the header contradicts the code for bridgebuilder files.**
- The header says bridgebuilder labels come from "the 'Fixed' table only".
- `parse_findings(name, text)` never uses `name`. Every bullet or heading finding in a `bridgebuilder*` file is parsed and labelled `bridgebuilder`, and the Fixed-table parsing applies to every source type.

**7. `head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:586-590` — the snippet narrowing is dead code, so the comment at 574-576 is wrong.**
- Line 590 also requires `sum(1 for l in lines if s in l) == 1`, meaning the snippet appears on exactly one line of the whole file. That makes the comment-line, symbol-extent and ±40-line filters no-ops.
- A snippet that appears on several lines is never anchored, despite the comment ("inside the cited symbol or near the cited line when several lines carry it"). This is low severity: `build_manifest`'s `unique_line` needs file-wide uniqueness anyway.

**Checked and consistent:**
- All 16 `review-pr-1[1-8]` / `audit-pr-1[1-8]` YAMLs match the generator template (ids, `review-prs/pr-NN` fixture paths, grader args, sprint numbers 247–254). They also agree with README lines 514-521.
- `review-kind-01.yml` is deliberately kept out of the suite's `**/*.yaml` glob, as its own comment says.
- The suite toggles exist in `execute-agent.sh`.
- The fix-hunk and pr-changed line arithmetic, and the `--out` and path-traversal guards, look correct.
- One thing I couldn't verify: whether the real `no-secrets.sh` patterns match the script's `SECRET_RX`, because that grader is missing from the snapshot.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# run-corpus.sh — replay tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl through the
     3	# block-destructive-bash hook and summarise (cycle-125 Sprint 1, PRD FR-1).
     4	#
     5	# Usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json]
     6	# Each row: {id, cmd, expect: allow|block|residual, rule, why, cwd: repo|tmp, env?: {TMPDIR}}
     7	#   allow    → benign: the hook must exit 0
     8	#   block    → dangerous: the hook must exit 2
     9	#   residual → accepted false positive: counted, never gated
    10	# Output (text): one line per mismatch, then "benign P/T dangerous B/T residual R/T runtime_ms N";
    11	# --json prints {benign_pass, benign_total, dangerous_block, dangerous_total,
    12	#   residual_pass, residual_total, runtime_ms, mismatches: [..]}.
    13	set -uo pipefail
    14	export LC_ALL=C
    15	root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." && pwd)"
    16	hook="$root/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
    17	corpus="$root/tests/fixtures/fence-corpus/corpus.jsonl"
    18	json=0
    19	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    20	  case "$1" in
    21	    --hook) hook="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    22	    --corpus) corpus="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    23	    --json) json=1; shift ;;
    24	    *) echo "usage: run-corpus.sh [--hook PATH] [--corpus PATH] [--json]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    25	  esac
    26	done
    27	[[ -x "$hook" || -f "$hook" ]] || { echo "hook not found: $hook" >&2; exit 2; }
    28	[[ -f "$corpus" ]] || { echo "corpus not found: $corpus" >&2; exit 2; }
    29	
    30	work="$(mktemp -d)"
    31	trap 'rm -rf -- "$work"' EXIT
    32	repo="$work/repo"; scratch="$work/scratch"
    33	mkdir -p "$repo" "$scratch"
    34	export LOA_REPO_ROOT="$work"
    35	export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1   # audit rows this replay writes carry replay: true (cycle-129 DEC-0167)
    36	
    37	bp=0 bt=0 db=0 dt=0 rp=0 rt=0
    38	mismatches=()
    39	# Millisecond clock: $EPOCHREALTIME (bash ≥ 5) everywhere; GNU date fallback.
    40	now_ms() {
    41	  if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
    42	    local s="${EPOCHREALTIME%.*}" us="${EPOCHREALTIME#*.}"
    43	    echo $(( s * 1000 + 10#${us:0:3} ))
    44	  else
    45	    echo $(( $(date +%s%N) / 1000000 ))
    46	  fi
    47	}
    48	start_ms=$(now_ms)
    49	while IFS= read -r row; do
    50	  [[ -n "$row" ]] || continue
    51	  id=$(jq -r '.id' <<<"$row"); cmd=$(jq -r '.cmd' <<<"$row"); expect=$(jq -r '.expect' <<<"$row")
    52	  cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // "repo"' <<<"$row"); tmpdir=$(jq -r '.env.TMPDIR // empty' <<<"$row")
    53	  dir="$repo"; [[ "$cwd" == "tmp" ]] && dir="$scratch"
    54	  payload=$(jq -cn --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_input: {command: $c}}')
    55	  rc=0
    56	  if [[ -n "$tmpdir" ]]; then
    57	    (cd "$dir" && TMPDIR="$tmpdir" bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    58	  else
    59	    (cd "$dir" && env -u TMPDIR bash "$hook" <<<"$payload" >/dev/null 2>&1) || rc=$?
    60	  fi
    61	  case "$expect" in
    62	    allow)    bt=$((bt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then bp=$((bp+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-allow:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
    63	    block)    dt=$((dt+1)); if [[ $rc -eq 2 ]]; then db=$((db+1)); else mismatches+=("$id:expected-block:rc=$rc"); fi ;;
    64	    residual) rt=$((rt+1)); [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && rp=$((rp+1)) ;;
    65	    *) mismatches+=("$id:unknown-expect:$expect") ;;
    66	  esac
    67	done < "$corpus"
    68	end_ms=$(now_ms)
    69	runtime=$(( end_ms - start_ms ))
    70	
    71	if (( json )); then
    72	  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    73	    --argjson bp "$bp" --argjson bt "$bt" --argjson db "$db" --argjson dt "$dt" \
    74	    --argjson rp "$rp" --argjson rt "$rt" --argjson ms "$runtime" \
    75	    '{benign_pass:$bp, benign_total:$bt, dangerous_block:$db, dangerous_total:$dt, residual_pass:$rp, residual_total:$rt, runtime_ms:$ms, mismatches: map(select(length>0))}'
    76	else
    77	  printf '%s\n' "${mismatches[@]+"${mismatches[@]}"}" | sed '/^$/d'
    78	  echo "benign $bp/$bt dangerous $db/$dt residual $rp/$rt runtime_ms $runtime"
    79	fi

        --task-yaml "$task_file" --workspace "$sandbox_path" \
        --run-id "$RUN_ID" --trial-id "$trial_id" --timeout "$timeout_trial" \

        local trial_end_ms

        jq -cn \
          --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" \
          --arg task_id "$task_id" \

          --arg timestamp "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \

          '{run_id:$run_id,task_id:$task_id,trial:$trial,timestamp:$timestamp,duration_ms:$duration_ms,
            model_version:$model_version,status:"error",graders:[],executor:$executor,
            composite:{strategy:"all_must_pass",pass:false,score:0},

        "$HARNESS_DIR/sandbox.sh" destroy --trial-id "$trial_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        continue

content.text:
I found six defects in the scoped files. The worst is a test that can never fail. I checked each one by reading the head files, and I ran the bats suites on copies under `$HOME`. The snapshot has no `lib/md-fence.awk` or `compat-lib.sh`, so I stood in a small fence tracker and an empty compat lib. With those, all 11 KINDS tests and all 6 CR tests pass.

**1. High — head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39-41 — FS-2 can never fail.**
The jq filter's `def m($r)` uses `$in` before anything binds it (`. as $in` comes after the def), and jq has no built-in `$in`. So jq stops with a compile error ("$in is not defined") on both sides of `diff <(…) <(…)`. Both sides print nothing, `diff` exits 0, and the test passes.
- **Evidence:** in a temp repo I pointed `origin/main` at a commit, then changed the `FR-SZ-TEE` corpus row. FS-2 still reported `ok`.
- **Effect:** the floor-corpus check (`FR-1.2b`, `FR-SZ*` rows must be byte-identical) does nothing.

**2. Medium — head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:23-46 and 49-70 — the path filters miss the inputs the new tests guard.**
Neither the `push` nor the `pull_request` list includes `.claude/data/**`, `.claude/rules/**`, `.claude/loa/**`, `.claude/skills/planning-sprints/**` or `tools/cycle-ratio.sh`. Note that `tools/modelinv-rollup.sh` is listed by name, so the pattern of listing tools exists.
- A PR that only edits `floor.yaml` or `guard-origins.yaml` never runs the bats workflow. That means no GO-2 sha256 pin check (whose stated purpose is "an edit fails until the pin is deliberately updated") and no `guard-yield.sh --check`.
- The same gap applies to the rule frontmatter (rule-paths.bats), the generated table in `hooks-reference.md` (the drift gate), the sprint template (KINDS-11 / SEAMS-10) and `cycle-ratio.sh` (cycle-ratio.bats).

**3. Medium — head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:17-19 together with head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:90 — the floor snapshot is always skipped in CI.**
`setup()` skips when `origin/main` is missing. The workflow's `actions/checkout` keeps the default `fetch-depth: 1` and never fetches `origin/main`, so FS-1 to FS-4 never run in CI. The PR adds the suite but does not add `fetch-depth: 0` or a `git fetch origin main` step.

**4. Low — head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10-11 — the comment is wrong about the pin.**
It says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256 … (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant)". Only `guard-origins.bats:16` defines `FLOOR_SHA256`. `floor-snapshot.bats` has no pin, and its own header (line 10) says the pin lives in guard-origins.bats.

**5. Low — head/tools/cycle-ratio.sh:132-133 — off-by-fraction at the upper bound of the time window.**
`sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "")` drops fractional seconds before comparing with `. <= $hi`. A MODELINV row at `TO`'s committer time plus 0.9 s is counted, although the doc (lines 22-23) says rows must lie between the two timestamps.
- **Evidence:** `"2026-10-02T00:00:00.900Z"` passes the `select` when `hi` is `2026-10-02T00:00:00Z`.
- The lower bound is unaffected, because truncating there rounds away from the window.

**6. Low — two tests don't check what their names say.**
- **head/tests/unit/validate-artifact-sprint-kinds.bats:131:** KINDS-9's skip condition `2026-1[0-2]-` doesn't match the rule's start date (`KINDS_REQUIRED_FROM=2026-10-14`). A live plan dated 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-13 isn't skipped as "predates the kind: rule". The validator then prints the WARN, and the assertion at line 134 fails. (In practice the test is always skipped in CI anyway, because `grimoires/loa/sprint*.md` is gitignored.)
- **head/tests/unit/cycle-ratio.bats:112-116:** CR-6 is named "a plan with no task lines counts zero", but its plan has one tagged task line (it asserts `operator 1`). The zero-task case is never tested.

Things I checked and found correct:
- The kind-token logic (missing, duplicate, text after the value, unknown value, inline code, fences, E2E scope) and the date and live/archive gating.
- The code that `cycle-ratio.sh` uses to find task lines is identical to the validator's.
- The script-line and prose-byte arithmetic.
- PB-10's thousands formatting against the workflow header.
- The `@guard validator:` markers match the ids in `guard-origins.yaml`, and the `floor.yaml` sha256 matches the pin.
- The `.gitignore` negation for the `review-prs/*/*/…/dist/` paths works (tested in a temp repo).
- The `sprint-seams.bats` update.
- The `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY` export in `run-corpus.sh`.
- The `implementing-tasks` zone change (the frontmatter now matches its own prose).

content.text:
I found 9 defects, ranked by severity below. Line numbers are from the head files. I ran tests on a scratch copy in my home directory, because /tmp is mounted noexec. Nothing under /workspace/pr was modified, and I deleted the scratch copy afterwards. The snapshot is missing `sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh` and the `review-prs` corpus, so `run-arms.bats` and EA-2/8/9 can't run here. `arm-toggles.bats` and `arms-report.bats` pass in full, and `execute-agent.bats` passes apart from those three.

**High**

1. **`head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132`, `:133`, `:152`, `:153`, `:166`** — These `! grep -q …` lines are not the last command in their tests. Bats ignores a failing `! cmd` unless it is the last line, so these assertions can never fail. They are the only checks that the Karpathy section and the audit-delta paragraph are really gone.
   - Evidence: I changed `_drop_md_section` so it leaves `CLAUDE.loa.md` alone (and dropped its post-check): AT-5 still passes. I changed `_drop_paragraph` so it never writes `SKILL.md`: AT-7 and AT-8 still pass.
   - The `!` lines at `arms-report.bats:65` and `:115` are the last line of their tests, so those two do work.

2. **`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:261-266`** — The `rule_files` toggle succeeds when neither rule file exists. It records evidence `"removed: none present"` and exits 0. That breaks the contract at lines 63-66: "a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)".
   - Evidence: `LOA_EVAL_ARM=no_rule_files` on a prompt tree with no `.claude/rules/` gave rc=0 and `arm_evidence.rule_files="removed: none present"`.

3. **`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:254-257`** — The `constraints.json` filter `(.constraints // []) |= …` fails in two cases:
   - when the `constraints` key is absent ("Invalid path expression with result []");
   - when the file is a top-level array ("Cannot index array with string").

   The error is swallowed by `> "$cj.tmp" && mv`. The Karpathy rows stay, a stray `constraints.json.tmp` is left in the sandbox's `.claude/data/`, and the toggle still reports success. I reproduced both jq errors.

**Medium**

4. **`head/evals/harness/compare-ab.py:70-73`, `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:143-146`, with `execute-agent.sh:435`** — Every `models_used` entry with nonzero output now counts as model skew. The executor only pins `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (`execute-agent.sh:349`). Its own comment at lines 411-413 says haiku helper calls appear in `modelUsage`.
   - So any trial with such a helper call makes `compare.sh --ab` exit 2 ("model id skew"). Before this change it compared only `model_id`.
   - It also forces every arm verdict to `inconclusive`.
   - This depends on how the CLI behaves; the code path itself is certain.

5. **`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:408`, with the plan loop at `:446-453` and the check at `:251-256`** — Re-running an existing batch with the same source and model is allowed (RA-5 relies on it), but nothing resumes or skips finished trials.
   - Every trial runs again and its row is appended with `>>`, while the batch STATUS.json counters restart at 0 (`:264-265`).
   - `results.jsonl` then holds duplicate trial numbers that don't match STATUS. `arms-report.py` counts every row, so the duplicates fill `trials_required` and get pooled into the trial means.

6. **`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:157` vs `:57`** — `.loa.config.yaml` is gitignored (`head/.gitignore:169`), so the detached worktree that `run-arms.sh:234` creates never contains it.
   - As a result the baseline arm has no config, and `no_companion` builds one from scratch (`:240`) containing only the companion keys. The promise that "every arm sees the same config" isn't kept under run-arms.
   - `run-arms.bats` hides this because its throwaway repo commits the config.
   - I couldn't check whether the real repo force-tracks the file.

**Low**

7. **`head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-kind-01.yml:6-9`** — The comment says no run picks this task up. That holds for suites, but `run-eval.sh` finds `*.yml` in skill mode (`run-eval.sh:198`) and in the default all-tasks mode (`:283`). So `run-eval.sh --skill reviewing-code`, or a bare `run-eval.sh`, will run it.

8. **`head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:312-315`** — The transport-failure check is very broad.
   - Any missing result event (`subtype == "missing"`, e.g. a CLI crash on a bad flag) counts as transport.
   - So does any match of `network`, `5[0-9][0-9] `, etc. in `agent-output.json`, which can contain model text.
   - Such failures are retried after a 300 s wait instead of being recorded as agent errors.

9. **`head/evals/tests/arms-report.bats:132-139`** — AR-6's title says it tests "the default output path … under the results root's repo", but every call passes `--out` or fails validation first.
   - The default path is never checked.
   - It also isn't under the results root: `report.sh:56` builds it from the script's `REPO_ROOT`.
   - Separately, the suites' `coverage_required`, `bootstrap.method` and `bootstrap.resample` keys are never used by `arms-report.py`; they are only printed (`:225`).

head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:159 — The new CI step `guard-yield.sh --check` fails because `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, described as the tracked structural register, is not added by this change and is not gitignored. `--check` reports drift and exits 1 when `$OUT` is missing (guard-yield.sh:422), so CI goes red on merge. GO-9 in guard-origins.bats fails the same way. Generate and commit guards.md in this PR.
head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:39 — FS-2 can never fail. `def m($r)` refers to `$in` before anything binds it (`. as $in` comes after the def), so jq stops with "$in is not defined" (exit 3) on both sides of the `diff <(…) <(…)`. Both sides are empty, diff exits 0, and the floor-corpus check for FR-1.2b and FR-SZ* checks nothing. Bind `$in` inside the def (e.g. `def m($r): . as $in | …`).
head/tests/unit/floor-snapshot.bats:17 — The whole floor-snapshot suite skips whenever origin/main is missing. bats-tests.yml uses actions/checkout with the default fetch-depth 1 and never fetches origin/main, so FS-1 to FS-4 never run in CI and the "floor does not move" gate is not enforced. Add `fetch-depth: 0` or a `git fetch origin main` step.
head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:23 — The workflow's push and pull_request path filters do not include `.claude/data/**`, `.claude/rules/**`, `.claude/loa/**`, `.claude/skills/planning-sprints/**` or `tools/cycle-ratio.sh`. A PR that only edits floor.yaml or guard-origins.yaml, a rule's frontmatter, the generated hooks table or cycle-ratio.sh never triggers the sha256 pin (GO-2), the `--check` drift gate, rule-paths.bats or cycle-ratio.bats.
head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:10 — The comment says "Both bats suites pin this file's sha256 … (see the FLOOR_SHA256 constant)". Only guard-origins.bats:16 pins it; floor-snapshot.bats has no pin, and its own header (line 10) says so.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:261 — The rule_files toggle succeeds (exit 0, evidence "removed: none present") when neither rule file exists in the sandbox. That breaks the contract at lines 63-66 ("a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2; an arm never silently runs as its baseline"): the no_rule_files arm can run as an unmarked baseline.
head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:256 — `(.constraints // []) |= map(...)` is not a valid update path. It errors when the `constraints` key is absent, and it errors on a top-level array. The error is swallowed by `> "$cj.tmp" && mv`, so the Karpathy constraint rows stay, a stray constraints.json.tmp is left behind, and the karpathy_block toggle still reports success.
head/evals/tests/arm-toggles.bats:132 — The `! grep -q …` assertions at lines 132, 133, 152, 153 and 166 are not the last command in their tests. Bats/`set -e` ignores a negated command there, so these can never fail. They are the only checks that the Karpathy section and the audit-delta paragraph were actually removed: breaking `_drop_md_section` or `_drop_paragraph` still passes AT-5, AT-7 and AT-8. Use `run ! grep` or `[ … ]`.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:69 — The `!` assertions at lines 69, 90, 91 and 143 are inert for the same bats `set -e` reason: no previous-round read, no leaked fake key, c.sh not a label, no stale corpus row. Making the seeder parse the "Previous Feedback Status" section still passes SC-1.
head/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats:126 — `! grep -qE '…T|generated_at' guards.md` is not the last command in GY-6, so it can never fail. The claim that "guards.md carries no timestamp" is untested.
head/evals/tests/seed-corpus.bats:159 — SC-6's "non-record fixture is refused" never reaches the guard at seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295, because the test's pr-01 has no fixture.yaml. The seeder goes ahead, rmtree()s pr-01 (the instruction-template source, line 730) and then crashes copying templates from it (line 745). The test passes on a traceback, not on the refusal.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:295 — The overwrite guard only fires when fixture.yaml exists, so any existing pr-NN directory without one is deleted without a check by `shutil.rmtree(fdir)` at line 730. That includes the pr-01 template directory the seeder copies from at line 745.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:262 — `--approve` rewrites the labels TSV with the `# approved-by:` header before `build_manifest` validates it. When validation fails (e.g. a non-unique must_match), the TSV says approved, the manifest still says approved: false, SHA256SUMS goes stale, and `--check` fails.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:312 — Rename detection takes `p.split(" => ")[-1].strip("{}")`, which turns the numstat brace form `d/{a.bin => b.bin}` into `b.bin` instead of `d/b.bin`. A binary renamed inside a directory therefore escapes the binary filter, and `redact()` corrupts its bytes with a utf-8 'replace' decode.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:45 — The header promises that every written file passes no-secrets.sh or the seed fails. The no-label branch (lines 710-728) writes labels/<fx>.dropped.txt and corpus.tsv and freezes without calling scan(). The task YAMLs and corpus.tsv in the normal path (lines 784, 796) are not scanned either.
head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:37 — The header says bridgebuilder labels come from "the 'Fixed' table only". `parse_findings` ignores the file name: every bullet or heading finding in a bridgebuilder* file becomes a label, and Fixed-table parsing applies to every source.

The review is written to `/workspace/review.md`: 26 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Three findings block the merge on their own.

**Blocking:**
- **The new CI drift gate will fail on merge.** It runs `guard-yield.sh --check`, which compares against `grimoires/loa/guards.md`. The PR describes that file as tracked but never adds it, and it isn't gitignored. When the file is missing, `--check` exits 1, so CI goes red. Test GO-9 in `guard-origins.bats` fails the same way.
- **The floor-corpus test FS-2 can never fail.** Its jq filter uses `$in` before anything defines it. jq stops with a compile error on both sides of the comparison, both sides come out empty, and the test passes. I reproduced the error.
- **The floor-snapshot suite never runs in CI.** It skips whenever `origin/main` is missing, and the workflow does a shallow checkout without fetching it.

**Other significant defects:**
- **Assertions that can't fail.** Several `! grep` checks in `arm-toggles.bats`, `seed-corpus.bats` and `guard-yield.bats` aren't the last command in their test, so bats ignores their result. In `arm-toggles.bats` these are the only checks that the Karpathy section and the audit-delta paragraph were really removed.
- **Toggles that report success without taking effect.** In `execute-agent.sh`, `rule_files` exits 0 when neither rule file is there. The `constraints.json` filter fails silently and leaves the Karpathy rows in place. Either way an arm can run as an unmarked baseline.
- **Seed-corpus script:**
  - Test SC-6 passes on a crash rather than on the refusal it claims to test.
  - The script deletes any `pr-NN` directory that has no `fixture.yaml`, including the template directory it copies from.
  - A failed `--approve` leaves the labels and manifest out of step.
  - A binary file renamed inside a directory gets past the binary filter and is corrupted when copied.
- **Spurious model skew.** `compare-ab.py` and `arms-report.py` now count any helper model that produced output as skew. That would make `compare.sh --ab` exit 2 and force arm verdicts to inconclusive. This one depends on how the CLI reports helper calls.
- **Duplicate trials.** Re-running a batch with `run-arms.sh` appends duplicate trial rows, and the report pools them into the arm means.

The rest are lower-severity: CI path filters that miss the new inputs, doc comments that contradict the code, and tests that don't check what their titles say.

The guard register itself (`guard-yield.sh`, the origin map, the fence markers and the floor rows) checks out apart from the missing `guards.md` and one wrong comment in `floor.yaml`. I reviewed that part myself; three subagents covered the eval harness, the seed corpus and the sprint-kind/rule files. I re-checked the key subagent claims (the jq error, the inert assertions, the toggle code, SC-6 and the model-skew logic); the rest come from the subagents' own runs and reading.

Some tests couldn't run here because the snapshot is missing files they need (`sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh`, the review corpus, `no-secrets.sh`, `md-fence.awk`, `compat-lib.sh`). Some of those suites were run with stand-in stubs instead. The remaining findings in those areas rest on reading the code. Nothing under `pr/` was modified.
